sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A proposal to news editors: more revenue from the read, not the subscription, with free client-side code.
sections.para: And the associations to talk to.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Journalism is a business; subscriptions hit a ceiling; micropayments failed; pay by the read; not proven yet.

sections.label: Journalism is a business
sections.line: Around 300 UK local titles closed since 2005; 171 of 308 Portuguese municipalities at risk.
sections.para: Local journalism is the heart of it.

sections.label: Why subscriptions are not enough
sections.line: About 10% pay for online news in the UK, 8% in Portugal; most say they never will.
sections.para: One article, three subscriptions, nothing paid.

sections.label: What micropayments taught us
sections.line: Blendle, Coil, Axate and Google's Offerwall: friction sank the early ones; agents are a new reader.

sections.label: Our model: pay by the read
sections.line: £5 of credit, a few pence a page, charged by the share read, never blocked, all in the browser.
sections.para: Free for any publisher; PrompTugal.news runs it.

sections.label: Four ways to earn from it
sections.line: The meter, a revenue share via PrompTugal.news, licences to quote, agents paying at the source.
sections.para: Provenance says whose story it is.

sections.label: A workflow for one newsroom
sections.line: One regional story read on its own site and carried by PrompTugal.news, a share paid back.

sections.label: What we do not have yet
sections.line: Not proven: our revenue is small because our traffic is; we need partners with readers.

sections.label: Who we should talk to
sections.line: NMA, ICNN, PINF and the Society of Editors; API, AIIC, APMEDIO and ERC; News Media Europe and others.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Not proven at scale; the revenue share is a proposal; others' figures as reported.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Press Gazette, PINF, LabCom, Reuters Institute, Piano, TollBit and others, and earlier articles.
